title: THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE
text:

NEWSPAPER PUBLICITY.—Advance newspaper publicity for the reunion was generous. The largest amount of space was, naturally, given by The Savoy Star. In December, 1937, the Thirty-fifth Anniversary edition, with an entire section devoted to the College, was given wide circulation.

Earlier, when it was thought that the gymnasium would be completed during the fall, Mr. Gee sent notice of the forthcoming reunion to several papers for advance promotion. As it turned out, the issue was perhaps more effective in turning minds to the reunion, however.

Quite a lot of advance reunion publicity appeared in The Dallas Morning News, which carried pictures of two Savoy College men (now Dallas residents), E. A. McMahon, and and former student, and the George Elliot Coleric, the rather brief biography of Savoy College's early days.

One article of unusual news interest is quoted below as it was furbished to the Dallas Journal from Mr. Gus W. Thomasson of Dallas on July 29, 1938:

The article in the Dallas Journal of August 3, 1937, describing the interesting story was: (1937-1938)

SAVOY GYMNASIUM IS SUBJECT OF FIRST PRINTED PICTURE EVER SENT FROM TEXAS TOWN

The Journal is permitted to announce the introduction of the first photograph ever sent over telephone wires from one Texas point to another in the state's newspaper.

The picture was made in Savoy, Texas, about eleven o'clock this morning by Karl Moore, staff photographer of The Journal. Mr. Moore left Dallas this morning with The Journal's new portable wired picture machine. After taking the picture at Savoy, developed it and mounted it, he placed the print on the cylinder of the portable, hooked it up to a long distance telephone, called The Journal dark room and began sending the pictures.
